layers.note: A low, mat-forming herb of dry open slopes and gravel.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about −15 to 4 °C; gone below −25 °C and above 8 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −38 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −45 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 10 to 26 °C; gone below 7 °C, where summers are too short, and above 30 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 900 to 5,500 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 500.

degree_days_5.note: About 250 to 3,500 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 100.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.15, gone by 0.08.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit: summer-dry Cascade summers suit it; up to about 0.5 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone by 0.7.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (Paradise, about 1,650 m) from general knowledge of the species; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Sulphur buckwheat grows across the western mountains from British Columbia to California and Colorado (the PLANTS Database). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
